blocks.heading: Identify needs, design and review
blocks.text: A business identifies customer needs through relevant research, sales patterns, feedback and observation. It then decides which customers to serve and designs a suitable product or service, price and access. A stated preference is not a guaranteed sale: affordability, competing products and the buying situation matter. Test a feasible offering and use feedback to improve it. Customer focus does not require accepting every request at any cost. A change must fit resources and earn sufficient revenue for the enterprise’s purpose. Customer needs can change, so an initial survey does not remove the need to review actual behaviour.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Omi Lunches learns that workers need portable meals collected quickly during a short break. A suitable response could combine secure packaging, a collection time and an affordable price, then review actual orders and complaints. Advertising the old slow service would not address the stated need.
